Diagnostic with no recipe change, so the metrics equal the tip's. Prior stem-truncation savings suggest non-GEMM kernels are a large share of the step.
E006 favored Muon, so SGD likely loses 0.3 pp or more. It saves only the Newton-Schulz overhead, about 2-3%.

W2 (empirical), after E038. Tip is E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. E038 re-ran the same recipe on fresh seeds 13-22 and gave 0.7525. Held-out means keep landing 0.1-0.2 pp under the seeds 0-2 mean. The population mean is therefore about 0.752, and the official 0.75 bar has only about 0.2 pp of headroom.

Mechanisms, each tied to measured runs:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 stacked a freeze with +0.5 epoch and saved 0.40 s versus E027 at about 0 pp.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. Time-neutral boosters have failed about 8 times (E025, E029, E030, E032, wd, LS, and others). Averaging, LR shape and wd sit at a flat optimum within noise (about ±0.2 pp).
3. Time tracks pixels. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 28 and 32 px phases carry the accuracy (E018, E024).
4. Backward truncation on memory-bound large maps is the best lever (E028, E034, E036). E037 moved the freeze to 60%. It saved 0.25 s but cost 0.38 pp, about 0.65 s per pp, which is near break-even against the epoch dial. Stem trims are near exhausted.
5. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: I overpredicted time on trims and freezes, since the savings were larger than modelled. I was too optimistic on time-neutral accuracy gains. Accuracy ranges mostly held, except where the change cut training signal (E030, E032, E037).

Unsure: whether BN folding (I057) removes enough memory traffic to matter. The effect of replacing Muon with SGD is uncertain, and E006 suggests losing Muon costs accuracy. I can't judge the PCIe transfer of the bandwidth-bound levers, because it was never measured here. The tip is probably near the Pareto front for this architecture, and further trims need an accuracy refund paid in epochs."
